description: Helps you decide how to build an ROI case the buyer's finance team can check. You give your solution, its main value driver and the buyer's own figures: an annual value estimate, or current annual cost with the expected improvement percent. With them you get the ROI, payback, three year value and sensitivity. Without them it shows no ROI: it names the inputs to add and gives the structure of the case (the cost lines to price, your quoted results as reference points, the questions to ask). Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Missing required fields or invalid values return an error naming what to supply or correct. Use this instead of pricing_negotiation_guide when you need a buyer-checkable financial case before negotiating terms. Ask finance for the cash-only annual benefit when an investment decision depends on cash.

annual_cash_benefit.description: Optional buyer-confirmed annual cash benefit in US dollars, excluding staff time without a cash release. Ask finance to separate cash from non-cash value. Compared with the annual solution price; a cash deficit holds the investment decision. Format is a JSON number. For example, 30.

annual_revenue.description: Customer annual revenue. Shown as your input; it is not turned into a value. Format is a JSON number. For example, 24000.

annual_value_estimate.description: Optional: the buyer's own estimate of the annual value in dollars; used as the value when given. Format is a JSON number. For example, 24000.

company_size.description: Company size tier. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "startup".

current_annual_cost.description: Optional: what the problem or the current process costs the buyer a year, in dollars (their figure). Format is a JSON number. For example, 24000.

current_process.description: How they do it today. Separate the ways of working with a semicolon: each becomes a cost line to price. Not used in the calculation. Format is text. For example, "manual invoice review".

customer_name.description: Customer/prospect name. Format is text. For example, "an approved anonymous manufacturer".

employee_count.description: Number of employees. Shown as your input; it is not turned into a value. Format is a JSON number. For example, 12.

expected_improvement_percent.description: Optional: the share of that annual cost the buyer expects to save, in percent (their figure). Format is a JSON number. For example, 30.

implementation_timeline.description: Expected implementation time. Shown in the output; not used in the calculation. Format is text. For example, "six weeks".

industry.description: The customer's industry, in any words. Used for wording and sector notes only: no industry figure is applied to the calculation. A return needs the buyer's own figures (annual value estimate, or current annual cost with expected improvement percent). Format is text. For example, "manufacturing".

known_metrics.description: Metrics the prospect shared, or results you can quote. Listed as reference points, never as the buyer's figures; to turn the buyer's figures into the value, give current annual cost and expected improvement percent, or annual value estimate. Format is text. For example, "median approval time measured monthly".

primary_value_driver.description: Primary value category. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "revenue_increase".

solution_price.description: Annual cost of your solution. Format is a JSON number. For example, 24000.

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "logistics_tech".

your_solution.description: Your product/solution. Format is text. For example, "invoice review service".

name: roi_business_case_builder
title: ROI Business Case Builder
